title: The provider guarantees only the shape; three checks and a person decide what is kept
aria: Billpod's reader sends an invoice and a Zod schema through the gateway's callJson; Gemini writes under that schema, which fixes only the shape of a reply that finishes normally. Three checks follow: layer 1 reads how the call ended, layer 2 parses and checks the whole answer, layer 3 checks each value and drops what fails, then the Swiss QR code's exact values win and a person confirms the draft. Each way a reply can go wrong is caught at one of these stages, and a call with no usable answer is not retried: the draft is built from the QR code and the matched recurring payment.
columns: One invoice reading, top to bottom

build.title: The reader asks; Gemini writes under the schema
build.text: Billpod's reader calls `callJson` with the PDF, a Zod schema and a 4096-token limit. Gemini gets the schema as `responseSchema` and fixes only the shape of a reply that finishes normally.

build.title: Four ways a reply goes wrong
build.text: JSON asked for in the prompt alone can come back wrapped or broken, cut off or refused, with an impossible value, or with a real but false value. The schema prevents only the first.

build.title: Layers 1 and 2 in the gateway
build.text: Layer 1 reads `finishReason` before parsing: SAFETY and the other blocked reasons stop here, even with HTTP 200. Layer 2 parses and checks the whole answer. A failure in either gets no retry, and the failed call is still billed.

build.title: Layer 3 drops bad values one by one
build.text: Each value meets its own rule: a real date, a 3-letter currency, an IBAN that passes mod 97. A field that fails is dropped; in the example, 5 of 8 fields are kept.

build.title: The QR code and a person decide
build.text: The Swiss QR code's exact values beat the model's. A real IBAN planted by hidden text passes mod 97, so only the QR code and the person who confirms the draft can stop it.

route.title: Send the shape with the request, not in the prompt
route.text: The reader defines the record once, in Zod, and calls `callJson` with 4096 tokens. The gateway turns it into Gemini's `responseSchema` and sends it in the request settings.

route.title: The provider lets the model write only tokens that fit
route.text: Before each token, the provider removes every candidate that would break the schema. A reply that finishes normally parses, but its values may still be wrong.

route.title: Layer one reads how the call ended
route.text: STOP is a normal finish, MAX_TOKENS a reply cut off, SAFETY a refusal sent with HTTP 200. The gateway throws on a refusal before it parses anything, and does not retry.

route.title: Layer two parses and checks the whole answer once
route.text: The gateway parses the text and checks it against the same loose Zod schema, so "2026-02-30" passes here. A failure throws `LlmOutputError`, and Billpod does not retry.

route.title: Layer three checks each value and drops what fails
route.text: A date must exist, a currency is three letters, an IBAN must pass mod 97. `dueDate` 2026-02-30 is dropped; the IBAN passes and is kept.

route.title: Let the exact QR code win over the model
route.text: For every field the QR code has, its value beats the model's: `iban = qr?.iban ?? ai?.iban`. Hidden white-on-white text cannot change an IBAN the QR code carries.

route.title: Hand a person a draft, never a bill
route.text: The draft shows each field's source: `qr`, `ai`, `recurring` or `none`. A person confirms or corrects it. On a bill without a QR code, only the person can catch a changed IBAN.
